proposition_tested: P3.2 Integration/AI assistance shifts review effort elsewhere rather than removing it; P1.3 Rework due to inaccurate output is a major driver (inside-frontier arm of the same experiment)
observed_finding: In the pre-registered field experiment with 758 BCG consultants, for 18 realistic consulting tasks inside the AI capability frontier, consultants with GPT-4 access completed more tasks, faster, and with higher-rated quality than controls; below-average performers gained most. For one task deliberately designed to be outside the frontier, AI users were less likely to be correct.
population_and_setting: 758 BCG individual-contributor consultants (~7% of that level); realistic consulting tasks; producers of analysis, not recipients reviewing outside work
study_or_observation_method: Randomized assignment to no AI / GPT-4 / GPT-4 + prompt-engineering overview after a baseline task
intervention_and_comparator: GPT-4 access (with or without prompt overview) vs no AI access
outcome_measured: Task completion, time, human-graded quality (inside frontier); binary correctness (outside frontier)
quantitative_result: Inside frontier: 12.2% more tasks completed on average, 25.1% more quickly, >40% higher quality vs control; below-average performers +43%, above-average +17% vs own baseline. Outside frontier: correctness ~84.5% control vs 60% and 70% in AI conditions (average -19 percentage points).
source_locator: Abstract (p.1); Section 3.1 'Quality and Productivity Booster - Inside the Frontier'; Section 3.2 'Quality Disruptor - Outside the frontier' (correctness paragraph, Figure 7, Table 4) — HBS Working Paper 24-013 as hosted at mitsloan.mit.edu
short_exact_excerpt: consultants using AI were significantly more productive (they completed 12.2% more tasks on average, and completed tasks 25.1% more quickly), and produced significantly higher quality results
limitations: Producer-side use of AI by consultants on their own tasks, not recipients reviewing outside analysis. Quality graded by humans; outside-frontier task deliberately designed so that GPT-4 would give a plausible but wrong answer (Section 3.2), so the -19 pp result is a constructed stress test, not a prevalence estimate. Working-paper version (2023); published version (Organization Science) not checked.
transferability_to_target_workflow: Mechanism analog only: advisor-side AI can raise output volume/quality on in-frontier tasks while degrading correctness on tasks where the AI is plausibly wrong. For renewable-energy diligence, needs verification of which diligence tasks are inside vs outside the frontier and whether recipients can tell. Differences: consultants are producers; no client review step was measured.
analyst_inference: Added by the coordinator to correct selective reporting flagged by R2C-01: the register previously contained only the outside-frontier arm. Read together, the two arms imply that rework risk (W3) is task-dependent and hard for producers to see, rather than uniformly high.
